versions.short: The bill would transfer management responsibility for two pieces of federal land in Tuolumne County, California, between two federal agencies. About 160 acres of Forest Service land would move to the Interior Department to be managed as part of Yosemite National Park under National Park System laws. About 170 acres of National Park System land would move to the Agriculture Department to be managed as part of Stanislaus National Forest under National Forest System laws. The bill would also let the two departments, by mutual agreement, make minor boundary corrections and adjustments, effective once they are published in the Federal Register. Existing rights, permits, leases, and easements on the land would not be affected, though the receiving agency would take over administering them under applicable law.
